newsitem.title: UK: Britain funds more mad cow studies.
newsitem.headline: Britain funds more mad cow studies.

text.p: Two British research agencies announced eight million pounds ($13 million) worth of new research into mad cow disease and its human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD) on Thursday.
The 23 separate projects include research into how closely the two diseases are related, how they are transmitted and whether any treatment is possible.
The government-funded Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC) and the Medical Research Council (MRC) will fund the studies.

Such research has taken on a greater priority since scientists announced last year they had identified a new variant of CJD and said it probably came from eating beef infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease).
Scientists have complained that a lack of funding hampered quick research into the illnesses.

CJD is normally a very rare brain-wasting disease that affects literally one in a million people. But there are fears that since the BSE epidemic in British cattle, which affected 165,000 animals before it was brought under control, that a similar epidemic could develop among humans.
Only 14 cases have been confirmed in Britain and one in France of the new variant, but CJD normally has a very long incubation period and the present cases could be the very beginning.
Scientists predict BSE will disappear early next century.
